strengths: Addresses a timely and underexplored question: whether feed-forward 3D foundation models (VGGT) internalize principled geometric reasoning (epipolar geometry, correspondence) versus relying purely on learned appearance priors, filling a genuine gap relative to prior interpretability work that has focused mostly on LLMs and discriminative vision models.

Methodologically thorough multi-pronged analysis: linear probing across layers, QK attention-space correspondence analysis, and causal attention-knockout interventions, with the supplementary providing increasingly localized interventions (whole-map -> patch-level -> individual correspondence) that meaningfully strengthen the causal claims beyond simple correlation.

Well-designed controlled synthetic benchmark with full ground truth (camera parameters, correspondences, fundamental/essential matrices) enabling precise, unconfounded probing that would be hard to obtain from real-world data.

The identification of a consistent transition point (~layer 10-14) where correspondence matching and epipolar-geometry decodability emerge together, corroborated by both Sampson error and rank-2 singular-value analysis, provides a coherent and internally consistent story.

Extensive robustness comparisons (occlusion, lighting/color, symmetry/repetition, focal length) against both classical (SIFT+RANSAC) and learned (SuperGlue+RANSAC) baselines give useful practical insight into VGGT's data-driven robustness and its failure modes (e.g., asymmetric lighting, shadow removal), including an interesting and candidly discussed 'hallucination' phenomenon under occlusion.

Authors are appropriately forthright about limitations (synthetic-only data, non-local interventions, confounds with classical baselines on texture-less renders, inability to prove correspondence heads are the sole cause of epipolar geometry).
weaknesses: All experiments are conducted on a small, fairly simple synthetic ShapeNet-rendered dataset (as few as 40 object instances across 10 categories); it remains unclear how well the mechanistic findings (layer localization, causal head roles) transfer to VGGT's behavior on complex real-world scenes with clutter, texture, and diverse camera trajectories it was actually trained on.

The study examines a single model (VGGT) only; no comparison to other feed-forward 3D reconstruction architectures (e.g., DUSt3R, MASt3R, VGGSfM) is provided, which would help establish whether the observed geometric emergence is a general property of this model family or specific to VGGT's particular training/architecture.

Probing is restricted to the camera token at each layer; patch/local tokens, which likely carry substantial correspondence and geometric information, are not probed, potentially underestimating or mischaracterizing where and how geometric information is distributed in the representation.

The causal interpretation remains only partially resolved: even with progressively localized attention knockouts, the paper cannot rule out that the implicated heads perform functions beyond correspondence matching that also contribute to the observed degradation (acknowledged by the authors themselves).

Comparisons with SIFT+RANSAC and SuperGlue+RANSAC baselines are potentially confounded by known weaknesses of these classical/local methods on synthetic, texture-poor renders, limiting the strength of the robustness claims about VGGT's superiority (also acknowledged as a limitation, but not mitigated by e.g. additional feature detectors or tuned classical pipelines).

Reported results are largely based on medians/aggregate statistics without confidence intervals or variance across scenes/objects, making it harder to judge the statistical robustness of the layer-wise transitions and intervention effects.
No explicit statement on code/dataset release for reproducibility is provided in the main text, which would be important given the custom synthetic dataset and analysis pipeline.

strengths: Addresses a timely and underexplored question: whether feed-forward 3D foundation models like VGGT internalize classical geometric principles (epipolar geometry, correspondence) versus relying on learned data priors.

The methodology combines complementary analysis techniques: layer-wise probing for the fundamental matrix, attention-map correspondence analysis, and causal attention-knockout interventions, which together build a reasonably coherent narrative connecting correspondence matching in mid-layers to emergent epipolar geometry.

The controlled synthetic ShapeNet-based dataset with full ground truth (camera poses, correspondences, fundamental/essential matrices) allows precise manipulation of occlusion, lighting, focal length, and symmetry, which is useful for the proposed interpretability study.

The localized intervention experiments in the supplementary (zeroing only corresponding-patch attention vs. whole attention maps) show appropriate self-awareness of confounds and attempt to isolate the causal role of correspondence matching specifically.

The paper is honest about limitations, e.g., acknowledging that interventions are not fully local and that hidden mechanisms in the same heads could also explain effects, and that SIFT may be disadvantaged on synthetic textureless data.
weaknesses: The evaluation is entirely on a small-scale, simplistic synthetic ShapeNet dataset (single isolated objects, Blender renders) with no validation on the real-world datasets VGGT was trained/evaluated on; this substantially limits confidence that the findings (layer localization, correspondence-geometry link, occlusion robustness) generalize to realistic scenes with clutter, texture, and multi-object complexity.

Core claims rest on correlational and coarse causal evidence: attention-knockout interventions zero out entire layer-head attention maps (even in the 'localized' supplementary variants, entire attention rows for a patch are zeroed), which is a blunt intervention that cannot cleanly disentangle correspondence-matching from other possible functions of those heads, a limitation the authors themselves admit but do not resolve.

The probing experiments use only the camera token and simple 2-layer MLPs to regress the fundamental matrix; the chosen metric (Sampson error layer-wise) is somewhat indirect for claiming 'the network encodes epipolar geometry' since an MLP probe with enough capacity could extract geometric information even from representations that do not explicitly encode it in a meaningful way (classic probe interpretability pitfall), and this concern is not discussed.

The attention-correspondence analysis uses a simple top-1 argmax matching criterion within discretized 14x14 patches, which is a coarse proxy for correspondence and does not account for multi-modal or distributed attention patterns that could still encode geometric relationships without concentrating in a single peak.

Comparisons against classical pipelines (SIFT+8-point+RANSAC, SuperGlue+RANSAC) may be somewhat unfair given the acknowledged issue that SIFT struggles on textureless synthetic renders, undermining the robustness claims that VGGT is superior to classical methods; the paper does not control for this confound quantitatively.

No comparison to other feed-forward models (DUSt3R, MASt3R, Fast3R) is performed despite these being discussed in related work and sharing similar architecture choices; the findings are specific to a single checkpoint of a single model, limiting the generality of claims about feed-forward 3D models as a class.

The paper's contribution is primarily analytical/observational (interpretability case study) without proposing new methods, improved architectures, or actionable techniques to mitigate the identified 'undesirable hallucination' behavior under occlusion, somewhat limiting its practical impact despite being an interesting scientific investigation.

Dataset size for several experiments is quite small (e.g., 5-40 scenes, 10-13 ShapeNet categories), which raises concerns about statistical robustness of the reported median errors and failure rates, especially given the high variance typically seen in geometric estimation tasks.

The writing in places over-claims certainty (e.g., 'This confirms our hypothesis') despite the paper's own acknowledgment that alternative explanations (other encoded mechanisms in the same heads) cannot be ruled out, creating some inconsistency between the strength of claims and the actual evidentiary support.

strengths: Addresses a timely and underexplored question—mechanistic interpretability of feed-forward 3D foundation models like VGGT—filling a clear gap relative to the extensive interpretability literature on LLMs and CNNs.

Methodologically thorough: combines linear probing, attention-map analysis, and causal attention-knockout interventions, moving beyond mere correlational claims to establish a causal link between mid-layer correspondence matching and epipolar geometry representation.

The supplementary ablations refining the intervention locality (whole-map knockout vs. correspondence-only patch knockout vs. single-correspondence knockout) show commendable rigor and self-critical validation of the main causal claim.

Well-designed, fully controlled synthetic ShapeNet-based dataset with complete ground truth (camera parameters, correspondences, fundamental matrices), enabling precise quantitative evaluation that would be infeasible with real-world data.

Comprehensive robustness study spanning occlusion, lighting/color changes, symmetric/ambiguous scenes, and focal length variation, with sensible comparisons to classical (SIFT+RANSAC) and learned (SuperGlue) baselines.

Honest and nuanced framing of results, including identification of a potentially undesirable 'hallucination' behavior under occlusion and clearly stated limitations regarding interpretive scope of the interventions.
Clear writing and logical structure, with each subsection building toward a coherent narrative (correlation → localization → causation → data-prior robustness).
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to two-view scenarios and synthetic ShapeNet objects; VGGT is designed for joint reasoning over many (up to hundreds of) views, so it remains unclear whether the identified mid-layer correspondence/epipolar mechanisms generalize to the multi-view regime that is VGGT's actual use case.

The analysis is limited to a single geometric quantity (the fundamental matrix/epipolar constraint); other core VGGT outputs (depth, 3D point tracks, absolute camera pose) are not probed, leaving open whether the observed 'geometric understanding' is specific to two-view epipolar structure or reflects a broader geometric competence.

Test sets in several experiments are quite small (e.g., 5-scene test set for correspondence/intervention analysis, 40 scenes for occlusion), and no statistical significance measures or variance estimates are reported, which limits confidence in the precise numeric findings (though the qualitative trends appear consistent).

No direct empirical comparison to the concurrent DUSt3R-focused interpretability work (Stary et al.) is provided, which would have helped situate the findings and assess whether the discovered mechanisms are specific to VGGT's architecture or common across feed-forward 3D transformers.

The attention-knockout intervention, even in its localized form, still cannot fully rule out that the implicated attention heads perform other latent computations besides correspondence matching, a limitation the authors acknowledge but do not fully resolve.

As a purely analytical/observational contribution (no new method, architecture, or benchmark proposed), the practical impact for downstream 3D vision applications is somewhat limited; the paper would benefit from more discussion of how these interpretability insights could inform future model design or failure diagnosis in practice.

strengths: Addresses a timely and important question—whether feed-forward 3D reconstruction models (DUSt3R, VGGT, DA3) internalize classical geometric principles (epipolar geometry, correspondence) or rely mainly on learned priors—which is valuable to the community given the rapid adoption of these foundation models.

Combines correlational evidence (layer-wise probing for the fundamental matrix, rank-2/singular-value checks, attention-map correspondence analysis, feature-similarity analysis) with causal evidence (attention-knockout interventions at four levels of locality), which is methodologically stronger than probing alone and helps substantiate the causal claim that correspondence-forming attention heads support the encoded epipolar geometry.

Broad empirical scope: three real-world datasets (DTU, ETH3D, MipNeRF360) plus a carefully constructed, fully-controlled synthetic ShapeNet dataset with ground-truth camera geometry, correspondences, and fundamental/essential matrices, enabling systematic manipulation of viewpoint, focal length, symmetry/repetition, and occlusion.

Findings are largely consistent across models and datasets (middle-layer emergence for VGGT/DA3, early-layer emergence for DUSt3R), lending credibility to the conclusions, and the extensive appendix (probe ablations, multi-view/triplet consistency, semantic correspondence, model-size sweeps for DA3, additional interventions) supports robustness of the central claims.

The robustness/learned-priors study (occlusion 'hallucination' behavior, lighting/color robustness, symmetric/repetitive scene failure, focal-length robustness) yields practically relevant insights, e.g., that VGGT partially reconstructs correspondences in occluded regions via learned priors rather than leaving them unmatched, which has direct implications for reliability in downstream 3D applications.
weaknesses: The contribution is primarily an empirical/interpretability analysis rather than a new algorithm, dataset, or theory; while this is a legitimate and useful contribution type, the insights delivered (models form correspondence-like attention structure that supports approximate epipolar geometry) are largely confirmatory of what one would expect rather than surprising, somewhat limiting novelty.

For DUSt3R, a large fraction (72%) of whole-head/image-map interventions produce invalid camera-pose predictions and are excluded from analysis, which weakens the strength and completeness of the causal claims for this model and suggests the intervention protocol may not transfer cleanly across architectures.

Baselines for the classical/learned-prior comparison (SIFT+8-point, SuperGlue) are relatively dated; more recent detector-free matchers (e.g., LoFTR, RoMa) mentioned in related work are not used in the comparative robustness experiments, which would have made the 'learned priors vs. classical pipelines' claims more convincing.

Many quantitative results (bar charts, heatmaps) are reported without error bars, statistical significance testing, or larger-scale ablations, making it harder to judge the reliability of some fine-grained trends (e.g., subtle inter-model differences in emergence layer, or the qualitative-only rank-2/singular-value evidence).

The synthetic dataset, while well controlled, consists of relatively simple, clean object-centric scenes; the occlusion/ambiguity findings, though interesting, are not validated on more complex real scenes with actual downstream reconstruction-quality metrics (only correspondence/Sampson-error proxies are used).

Several explanatory claims about architectural differences (e.g., why DA3 exhibits particular layer patterns, why VGGT's semantic-to-geometric transition occurs) are speculative ("we believe", "may stem from") without direct verification.
No explicit statement on code/data release is evident, which affects reproducibility of the fairly complex multi-model, multi-dataset analysis pipeline.

strengths: Addresses a timely and interesting question: whether feed-forward 3D reconstruction foundation models (DUSt3R, VGGT, Depth Anything 3) internalize classical multi-view geometric reasoning (epipolar geometry, correspondences) or rely primarily on learned data priors.

Methodologically diverse toolkit combining layer-wise probing of the fundamental matrix, attention-map correspondence analysis, and targeted causal interventions (attention knockout), going a step beyond pure correlational probing.

Construction of a controlled synthetic ShapeNet-based dataset with full geometric ground truth (poses, correspondences, F) allows systematic manipulation of focal length, baseline angle, symmetry/repetition, and occlusion—useful for isolating confounds that are hard to control in real data.

Reasonably broad empirical coverage across three real-world datasets (DTU, ETH3D, MipNeRF360) plus the synthetic set, and additional robustness studies (lighting/color, focal length, symmetric/repetitive scenes) that go beyond the core interpretability claims.

Some genuinely informative qualitative observations, e.g., the differing layer location of geometric emergence between camera-token architectures (VGGT/DA3) versus DUSt3R's asymmetric decoder, and the identification of partial correspondence 'hallucination' under occlusion.
weaknesses: The central finding—that intermediate representations encode recoverable epipolar geometry and that this correlates with correspondence-matching attention heads—is largely expected given these models are implicitly trained on multi-view correspondence tasks; the paper offers limited mechanistic insight beyond confirming this prior, and does not translate the findings into any actionable improvement to models or training.

Probing-based claims of 'geometric understanding' are subject to the well-known limitation that successful decoding by an MLP does not establish that the information is causally used by the network in a geometrically meaningful way; the paper does not include standard probing controls (e.g., control tasks, selectivity measures) to rule out the probe itself learning the task.

The causal attention-knockout experiments, while a step forward, are explicitly acknowledged by the authors to be confounded (disrupted heads may encode more than just correspondence), weakening the strength of the 'causal relationship' claims repeatedly asserted in the boxed takeaways throughout the paper.

For DUSt3R, 72% of intervened cases produce invalid camera-pose predictions under two of the four intervention types, and results are reported only on the remaining valid subset—this selection likely biases the comparison and undermines the cross-model comparability central to the paper's narrative.

Most quantitative results are presented purely qualitatively (visual trends in line/bar charts) without error bars, statistical tests, or confidence intervals, making it hard to assess the robustness and significance of the reported 'sudden transitions' and layer-wise trends.

The synthetic ShapeNet dataset used for the most tightly controlled experiments (probing, attention knockout) is fairly small (e.g., 15 train/2 val/2 test instances per category, 5–40 test scenes), raising concerns about the statistical reliability and generalizability of conclusions drawn from it.

The data-prior analysis in Section 5 is conducted only on VGGT, yet the discussion and conclusion generalize claims about 'learned priors' and 'hallucination under occlusion' to the broader class of feed-forward models without verifying these effects hold for DUSt3R and DA3.

Substantial portions of the technical content and most of the experiment variety (occlusion, lighting, symmetry, focal length robustness, semantic correspondence, multi-size DA3 comparison) are relegated to a lengthy appendix (14 pages) that is longer than the main paper, suggesting the core submission is thin and heavily dependent on supplementary material for completeness.

Closely related prior work (e.g., Stary et al. on layer/correspondence roles in multi-view transformers, Maggio et al. and Han et al. on VGGT layer analysis) already explores similar interpretability questions; the paper's incremental differentiation from this line of work is not clearly articulated beyond broader dataset/model coverage.

The occlusion 'hallucination' finding is interesting but shallow: the experiments show attention heads remain partially active on masked patches, but do not assess whether the resulting reconstructed geometry is actually correct or merely plausible-looking, limiting the practical significance of the claim.

strengths: Addresses a timely and important question for the field: whether feed-forward 3D reconstruction foundation models (DUSt3R, VGGT, Depth Anything 3) internalize classical geometric principles (epipolar geometry) or primarily rely on learned data priors.

Employs a multi-pronged methodology combining linear/MLP probing of intermediate representations, attention-pattern analysis for correspondence matching, and causal attention-knockout interventions at multiple localities (whole head, image map, block, patch), which together build a convincing case rather than relying on a single diagnostic.

Introduces a well-designed, fully-controlled synthetic ShapeNet-based dataset with exact ground-truth camera poses, correspondences, and fundamental/essential matrices, enabling precise manipulation of viewpoint, focal length, symmetry, and occlusion that would be impossible with real data alone.

Extensive experimental coverage: three real-world datasets (DTU, ETH3D, MipNeRF360) plus SPair71k for semantic correspondence, three model architectures, multiple DA3 model sizes, two-view and three-view settings, and multiple probe designs (linear vs. MLP, early-stopping ablations) that support the robustness of the reported trends.

The causal attention-knockout experiments (Sec. 4.3, App. D) go beyond correlational probing evidence and provide a genuine causal link between correspondence-encoding attention heads and the emergent epipolar-geometry representation.

The learned-prior robustness study (Sec. 5) offers nuanced, non-trivial findings, e.g., VGGT partially 'hallucinates' correspondences under occlusion (partially beneficial but sometimes undesirable) and outperforms classical/learned pipelines under lighting, focal-length, and moderate symmetry perturbations while still failing under fully symmetric/ambiguous configurations, mirroring the fundamental limits of multi-view geometry.

The paper is transparent about failure cases and limitations of its own causal claims (e.g., acknowledging that attention heads may encode more than correspondence, and that DUSt3R's cross-attention interventions frequently produce invalid poses), which strengthens the credibility of the analysis.
weaknesses: The learned-prior robustness study (Section 5) is conducted almost exclusively on VGGT; DUSt3R and DA3 are not evaluated under the same occlusion/lighting/symmetry perturbations, which limits how broadly the 'reliance on learned priors' conclusion can be generalized across all three studied architectures.

The causal interventions, while informative, are still somewhat coarse (zeroing full heads or spatial neighborhoods) and the authors themselves note this does not conclusively isolate correspondence matching as the sole mechanism responsible for epipolar-geometry encoding — some claims remain partially correlational despite the causal framing.

The custom ShapeNet dataset, though useful for control, consists of single objects against relatively simple backgrounds/rendered scenes, which may not fully capture the complexity (clutter, dynamic elements, real-world lighting/texture variation) present in the real deployment settings these models target; generalizability of fine-grained layer-wise findings to more complex real scenes is only partially validated via the real-world datasets.

The overall narrative conclusions (models partly learn geometry, but also rely heavily on data priors that aid in-distribution robustness yet can cause hallucination) are reasonable but largely confirmatory of prior intuitions in the field rather than delivering a strong surprising or actionable mechanistic insight (e.g., no concrete recommendation for architecture/training changes that would follow from the findings).

Dense multi-panel figures (e.g., Figs. 2, 3, 12, 16, 18) are visually cluttered and their axis labels are difficult to parse at the given resolution, which may hinder reproducibility/clarity for readers not consulting the supplementary material closely.

As an interpretability/analysis contribution (no new algorithm proposed), the paper's significance rests on the depth and reliability of its mechanistic claims; while the evidence is reasonably thorough, some conclusions (e.g., 'geometric phase transition,' 'inpainting-like' behavior) are somewhat speculative interpretations of the observed patterns rather than fully validated mechanisms.
